page: Amazon Web Services c6gn.xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System hypervisor. It is powered by 4 dedicated physical arm64 cores using the AWS Graviton Neoverse-N1 architecture operating at 2.5 GHz. Each core hosts a single thread without multithreading. The instance is allocated 8.0 GB of system RAM, maintaining a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio. It includes no local NVMe or drive storage, relying entirely on network-attached EBS volumes, and offers a baseline network bandwidth of 6 Gbps.

Performance testing reflects mixed results inherent to its arm64 microarchitecture profile. Single-core CPU tests in stress-ng score in the middle 50% average range (1519.39), as do large-block memory read and write throughput (72.78 GB/sec and 35.07 GB/sec respectively) and PassMark database operations (2626.26). However, multi-core CPU benchmarks, Geekbench workloads, small-block memory reads, and LLM prompt processing fall within lower performance categories. AES hardware encryption instructions are supported, while x86-specific instruction sets like AVX and AMX are omitted.

The c6gn.xlarge delivers cost efficiency for network-intensive and compute workloads optimized for ARM hardware that do not demand extensive RAM arrays or high local storage IOPS. Its 6 Gbps baseline network capacity coupled with dedicated ARM cores makes it effective for intermediate database processing, static web serving, software compilation tasks, and lightweight containerized microservices.
description: Amazon Web Services c6gn.xlarge is a compute-optimized ARM-based instance powered by a 4-core AWS Graviton Neoverse-N1 processor operating at 2.5 GHz. Built on the AWS Nitro System, it supplies 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, alongside 6 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth. The instance features no local instance storage and relies exclusively on remote EBS storage. Benchmark results place its single-core compute and large-block memory bandwidth in the middle performance tier, while multi-threaded integer and synthetic CPU scores fall in lower percentiles. Equipped with hardware AES instruction support but lacking x86 vector extensions, c6gn.xlarge is suitable for network-enhanced ARM applications, intermediate database processing, and lightweight microservices requiring dedicated physical vCPUs without extensive memory footprints.
